ENGINEER_SPECIES: an animate coal-suit with no one inside
a very old, very calm ghoul
a bugbear in a pressed uniform

spawn: Platform smells of ozone and old coffee. A souvenir stand sells hats.
Broken turnstiles, a working vending machine, and a sign reading NO REFUNDS.
A bench, a map with the wrong colors, and a clock that runs backwards.
Crawlers arrived here still holding their Floor 3 loot. Some of it is still on the tracks.
stairwell: Stairwell in the maintenance closet at the far end of the platform.
Stairwell disguised as the down escalator.
Stairwell at the bottom of a dead escalator.
Stairwell through the staff-only door at the end of the platform; the sign means it.
Stairwell under a mural of the line's opening day. The door is painted into the mural until it opens.
Stairwell behind the photo booth, which takes your picture every time you try the door early.
Stairwell in the middle of the concourse, behind a velvet rope and a sign: SIX HOURS.
transfer: Cross-platform transfer under a cracked glass roof.
Two platforms stacked; the stairs between them are the only way across.
A long tiled corridor between platforms, lit every third light.
Transfer through a shuttered concourse. The shops are closed, and not empty.
A spiral ramp between levels; the trains below can be heard long before they arrive.
A footbridge over the tracks. Something lives under it.
Transfer by a moving walkway that has not moved in years.
exit_cavern: Exit-only cavern. Mobs get their Rev-Up here; the 'rollercoaster' track at the back runs to the trainyard.
Exit-only cavern: a dispensary counter, a queue of twitching porters, and a rusted coaster rail.
Exit-only cavern. Whatever gets off here does not get back on this train.
safe_room: Safe room on the mezzanine between platforms.
Safe room is the old station pub; the taps still work.
Two platforms stacked; the safe room is the stationmaster's office between them.
Safe room doubles as the lost-and-found.
Safe room is a noodle counter with six stools and a proprietor who has seen everything.
Safe room in the old ticket hall; the ticket windows sell sandwiches now.
Safe room is a launderette. The machines are always mid-cycle.

NAMED_STOCK: a jet-black steam locomotive with a cowcatcher and forty cars
a sleek white maglev with a glass nose and two cars
a wooden funicular that should not be able to move on flat track
a double-decker diesel with the top deck missing
a hearse-black electric with velvet seats and no lights
a circus train, cages first, still painted
a hospital train with an operating car that is in use
a gold-plated dining train that is always mid-course
a freight train of sealed refrigerated cars
a children's park train, scaled up to full size, still playing its jingle
NAMED_ENTRY: Enter through the last car only; the doors between cars open one at a time toward the front.
Only the first car opens. It is empty. It is not empty.
Boards from the trackbed, not the platform. Jump.
Doors open for exactly eight seconds.
Entry requires a ticket sold by a conductor on any colored line. The conductor will not want to sell it.
NAMED_GIMMICK: The engineer's compartment is a boiler fed by a bound demon who will negotiate.
Triggers a quest on boarding: the crew wants the engineer dead and the engineer knows it.
Runs through the Abyss on every loop; the doors open over the pit.
Cars rearrange between stops. Count them.
Carries a working portal scoop on the front; can pull stranded crawlers off a platform at speed.
Every passenger is a crawler from a previous season, or something wearing one.
Stops for exactly one minute at each station on its loop, whether or not the station exists.
The last car is a mimic. It has been the last car for a very long time.
MIMIC_TELL: the announcements pronounce your name correctly
the station name changes when you look away
F4_STORY: The floor is a Syndicate logo when viewed from above. Nobody on the floor can view it from above.
The Rev-Up supply is being cut. The withdrawal timeline is the real countdown.
Trainyard crews remember home lives that do not match each other. They notice if asked.
An interdiction crash-response team was supposed to be stationed at 75. The station is empty. The cart is not.

pace.text: Dosed on schedule; holds at stage 1 almost to the end, then goes all at once.
The porters start missing their stops early, and the rest of the train follows them.
The engineer skims the supply. Cars 10 and 15 are not safe on this line.
A steady slide, a stage every few days.
The exit caverns on this line run dry first.
The crew ration their doses, so they decline late and hard.

symptoms: the shakes, and a short temper with anything in the way
they forget their stops, ride past them, and panic
an itch under the skin that they scratch down to the meat
they hear the announcements wrong and act on what they think they heard
sweats, cramps, and a habit of lunging at anyone who brushes past
they hoard: tickets, buttons, teeth, anything small
they stop sleeping, and doze on their feet mid-shift
everything tastes of rust, so they stop eating and start chewing
toll: about half of them don't come through it
one in three doesn't come through it
most come through it; the ones who don't die quietly, in their seats
a quarter don't come through it, mostly the old hands

risen.name: Seat Warmers
risen.does: slumped in their seats until the car fills, then they bite whoever sat nearest

risen.name: Last Stop Ghouls
risen.does: bloated and slow; they eat anything that was alive and drift toward others of their kind

risen.name: Commuter Husks
risen.does: they keep riding their old line, punching tickets that aren't there, and go for anyone without one

risen.name: Platform Sleepers
risen.does: they lie along the platform edge until a train comes in, then drag someone under it

risen.name: Gutter Ghouls
risen.does: they crawl the trackbed between stations and come up through the floor of the cars

risen.name: Lost Property
risen.does: the dead piled in a lost-and-found, who stand up as one when the room fills

symptoms: fast and strong, and no good at aiming any of it
they stop feeling pain, and stop slowing down for it
they start talking to each other, and stop talking to anyone else
they grow into their uniforms until the seams split
they move in rushes, a whole car at once, then go still
they forget who they were and keep only the job: a porter will carry anything, including you
toll: the strong ones survive it, which is the problem
it burns through them in a day or two

risen.name: Shift Ghouls
risen.does: ogre-sized and organized; they work in crews, and they still keep the timetable

risen.name: Brake Wraiths
risen.does: they ride the outside of the cars and peel crawlers off the roof

risen.name: Gangway Horrors
risen.does: they wedge into the gaps between cars and pull through anyone who tries to cross

risen.name: Union Dead
risen.does: they never fight alone: three or more, and they talk terms first, then rush

risen.name: Third Rail Ghouls
risen.does: they hug the live rail and come back up crackling

symptoms: they swell to the size of a car door and grow things out of their backs
they lose their faces, and then their need to breathe
they fuse to whatever they were sitting on and take it with them
their skin splits, and something grows in the gaps
they go perfectly calm, and then they don't
toll: it kills every one of them, and that is not the end of them

risen.name: Tunnel Grubs
risen.does: a burst of grubs no bigger than a fingernail that double in size every few hours; burn them early

risen.name: Wall Seedlings
risen.does: a spray of seeds that root in the tiles and sprout hands by morning

risen.name: Vent Brood
risen.does: a brood that scatters into the vents and comes back a size bigger every time it is seen

risen.name: Hatchlings
risen.does: the body splits open and the hatchlings go looking for something to live in

risen.name: Stage Spores
risen.does: a cloud that settles on anything breathing and pushes it a stage further along

last_day: The exit caverns stop dispensing. Every mob still aboard drops a stage within the hour.
Every train runs express for the end of the line and stops for nobody.
Whatever withdrawal raised starts moving toward the stairwell stations, all at once.
The crew stop pretending to work. Conductors leave car 5 and walk the train.
The platform lights go red and stay red, and the mobs take red as permission.
Trains start running both ways on the same track.
A supply cart runs every line one last time, and the mobs that reach it fight over the last doses.
The exit caverns seal. Mobs that get off can't get their fix, and can't get back on.
Every car's speakers count down the hours to collapse, and don't stop.
The yards empty: every train in them is sent out at once, crewed or not.

ghouls.name: Signal Ghouls
ghouls.does: they stand at the platform edge swinging lanterns, and trains stop for them, and so do crawlers who shouldn't

ghouls.name: Ticket Inspectors
ghouls.does: they ask to see your ticket. There is no right answer

ghouls.name: Stowaway Ghouls
ghouls.does: they ride folded into the luggage racks and drop on whoever sits beneath

ghouls.name: Crush Load
ghouls.does: a crowd of the dead that moves as one and fills any space it is let into

ghouls.name: Mind the Gap
ghouls.does: long-armed things that live in the gap between train and platform, as the signs always warned

ghouls.name: Night Shift
ghouls.does: they only move while the station lights are dimmed, and the lights dim every hour

feeds: Every mob that dies of withdrawal anywhere on the floor gets up here, a day later.
A birthing tank in the old signal box turns out one an hour, faster as collapse nears.
Every crawler who dies on the floor's lines adds one.
Every dose handed out at an exit cavern adds one: the supply feeds them too.
Each train that passes without stopping leaves one behind on the platform.
Nothing makes them here. They come: anything that dies within a few stations walks here to join them.
A broken vending machine in the concourse dispenses one whenever anyone feeds it gold.
The station's own speakers call them. One answers every announcement.
tides: A handful at first. They fill the platform by day {mid} and the concourse by day {late}.
Quiet until day {mid}, then they arrive by the trainload.
They drift in and out until day {early}, then stop leaving.
A few more every day, and none of them ever leave.
They double every two days, from day 1.
A dozen most days. Hundreds by day {late}, all at once, when the last line hits stage 3.
They only gather at night, and by day {mid} the station is never not night.
openings: They all turn toward the stairwell door at once.
They pack the stairwell room and will not give ground to anything but fire.
They ignore crawlers until the stairwell opens. Then crawlers are all they see.
They hold the stairwell door shut from the inside.
They queue for it. Anyone who pushes in is torn apart by the queue.
They go perfectly still six hours out. Any noise wakes the whole room.
They flee the stairwell and swarm the trains instead, so the trains are the danger.

merged.name: The Rush Hour
merged.does: every ghoul in the room pressed into one heaving body that fills the stairwell door

merged.name: The Commuter Mass
merged.does: a wall of arms and briefcases that rolls forward a yard at a time and does not stop

merged.name: Standing Room Only
merged.does: a column of the dead stacked to the ceiling that topples onto whatever it is aimed at

merged.name: Lost and Found
merged.does: a heap that reaches out with whichever arms are nearest and keeps whatever it catches

merged.name: The Terminus
merged.does: they build themselves into a station of their own, platform and all, and wait for someone to board
